summary.oneLiner: CEAT Limited, part of the RPG Group, is one of India's premier tyre manufacturers and among the world's top 20 tyre companies, serving passenger, two-wheeler, commercial and off-highway/specialty vehicle segments across 110+ countries.
summary.business: CEAT manufactures tyres, tubes and flaps for passenger cars, two-wheelers/three-wheelers, commercial vehicles (trucks/buses/light commercial vehicles), farm and off-highway/specialty vehicles, sold to OEMs, replacement-market customers (via dealers, distributors, retailers and service centres), commercial fleet operators and export customers. Following the September 2025 acquisition of the CAMSO compact construction off-highway tyres and tracks business from Michelin, the Company has broadened its presence in global specialty and off-highway markets.

currentContext.strengths: Scale: amongst the world's top 20 tyre manufacturers, with 6 manufacturing plants in India and output of 45+ million tyres|Deep distribution reach: 5,700+ dealers, ~50,000 sub-dealers, 1,115+ special channels across 615+ districts, described as comparable in depth to a consumer goods company|R&D and innovation: 214 cumulative patents filed (60 granted), dedicated R&D/testing infrastructure including a Frankfurt R&D centre, first tyre brand to win the Deming Grand Prize outside Japan and two WEF Global Lighthouse awards (Chennai, Halol)|Brand strength: ranked among the Top 10 strongest tyre brands globally (Brand Finance 2025)|Advanced/flexible manufacturing with 50% smart manufacturing lines and continued capacity/process-excellence investment|Sustainability integration (Net Zero 2050 ambition, EUDR-ready deforestation-free sourcing, S&P Global sustainability score placing CEAT in the top 4% of the auto components industry globally) supporting brand and customer relationships
currentContext.strategies: Scaling a diversified global platform — expanding international presence through overseas entities/distribution and integrating the CAMSO off-highway tyres and tracks business to diversify revenue across on-road and off-road mobility segments|Driving premiumisation across segments — investing in brand, product development and retail formats to grow higher-margin premium passenger-vehicle and high-performance commercial-vehicle categories|Strengthening innovation and EV readiness — product development, research, materials science and testing capability aligned to electric-mobility requirements (durability, load-bearing capacity, low-noise) and continued participation in EV OEM programmes|Enhancing manufacturing capability and efficiency — calibrated capex for capacity augmentation, automation, process improvement and energy efficiency to sustain high capacity utilisation|Leveraging digital transformation — building a centralised data platform, advanced analytics and enterprise-wide digital systems to improve operational visibility and responsiveness|Democratising AI capability across the organisation — strengthening data architecture, instituting AI governance and setting up AI labs to embed AI in workflows and decision-making|Maintaining cost discipline, pricing actions and capital efficiency to navigate near-term input-cost and geopolitical pressures while sustaining growth momentum|Sustainability embedded in the growth model through the Net Zero 2050 ambition, sustainable materials, responsible sourcing and EUDR readiness|The Company describes a disciplined and balanced approach to capital allocation aligned with growth, premiumisation and global expansion, directing capex toward capacity enhancement, technology upgrades and product development while maintaining financial prudence and balance-sheet strength; investments also support international distribution, CAMSO integration and digital infrastructure. Dividend recommendations follow the Company's Dividend Distribution Policy (no sum was proposed for transfer to General Reserve for FY 2025-26). The Board also sought member authorisation to raise Non-Convertible Debentures up to Rs. 1,000 crore on a private-placement basis, indicating continued willingness to use debt financing alongside internal accruals.
currentContext.expansion: CEAT continued to expand and upgrade manufacturing capacity in FY26 to support growth across passenger, premium and global segments, with a focus on capacity enhancement, debottlenecking, automation and digitisation across its six India plants (all EV-ready for tyre production). Announced/ongoing capacity initiatives include an increase in PCUV (passenger car/utility vehicle) capacity at the Chennai plant from approx. 95 Lakhs/annum to 130 Lakhs/annum by FY 2027-28, off-highway tyres-and-tracks (OHT) capacity of approximately 220 tonnes/day, and an increase in two-wheeler capacity at the Nagpur plant from 80,000 to 100,000 units. Investments are also directed at expanding automated tyre-handling and storage systems, finished-goods capacity, predictive maintenance, and enterprise digital/analytics platforms. Separately, the CAMSO off-highway tyres-and-tracks business acquired from Michelin (completed September 1, 2025) is being integrated to add off-highway/specialty capacity and new SKUs, complementing the existing specialty portfolio, with global ownership of the CAMSO brand vesting after an initial 3-year licensing period.
currentContext.mdna: Replacement and OEM demand supported by improving affordability following GST rationalisation and sustained demand momentum across categories|Long-term tyre industry outlook favoured by increasing vehicle penetration, infrastructure/economic activity growth, and ongoing premiumisation across segments|International business (Europe, United States and other key markets) contributing strongly to growth, with continued headroom for global expansion supported by a more diversified market presence|Market share gains across key replacement categories and deepening OEM engagement supporting mix and margin improvement|Rising raw material costs and supply-chain disruptions (including from the Iran conflict late in the year) weighed on the operating environment in the latter part of FY26|Input cost inflation flagged as a significant headwind entering FY 2026-27, tempering an otherwise resilient demand outlook|Increasing contribution of premium products in higher-end passenger vehicles and performance segments beginning to meaningfully influence product mix and margins

risks.risk: Raw material price volatility and competitive pricing pressure on margins
risks.note: Management flags margin impact from raw material price volatility and competitive pricing pressures as a key risk; mitigated via supplier diversification, strengthened OEM partnerships, cost optimisation across procurement/manufacturing/distribution, premiumisation and price discipline.
Identified as a key risk to the business; managed through periodic assessments, preventive and detective controls, external security experts, and a Data Recovery Plan for business continuity.

Flagged as a key risk given global tariff and geopolitical uncertainty (including supply-chain disruption from the Iran conflict during the year); mitigated through supply chain agility, balance-sheet monitoring and expansion into diversified geographies, OEMs and product segments.
A flagged macro risk; mitigation includes disciplined working capital and capex management, maintaining optimal leverage, improving cash flows and enhancing operational flexibility.

Integrating the CAMSO off-highway tyres-and-tracks business (acquired from Michelin) carries execution risk; the Company cites a structured integration framework with dedicated teams, supply chain harmonisation, global sourcing, cultural integration and phased systems integration as mitigants.

Listed as a threat in the Company's SWOT analysis, relevant given export turnover (19% of total turnover) and a growing multi-country subsidiary/JV footprint (USA, Europe, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, Indonesia, Brazil, UK).
Listed as a threat in the SWOT analysis, reflecting a competitive domestic and export tyre market that pressures pricing and market share.

one-line thesis: CEAT is outgrowing the tyre industry through aggressive premiumization, international expansion, and electrification, despite near-term margin pressure from surging natural rubber prices; the company is leveraging superior product quality and targeted marketing to capture high-value segments and improve profitability over the next 12-18 months.
financial scorecard: rev:+8.8% YoY; EBITDA:-1.3% YoY; PAT:+6.9% YoY; orderbook:Strong; netdebt:-343cr YoY
guidance: FY25 capex guidance of INR1,000cr maintained; international business to reach 25% of revenue in 2-3 years; raw material cost expected to rise 5-6% in Q2; pricing hikes of 3-4% cumulative needed to offset RM inflation; EPR provision to be treated as operational cost; no change to volume growth outlook of double-digit replacement and export growth.
order book & pipeline: TBR capacity at Halol fully sold out; strong order base in LATAM, Europe, and US; healthy demand in replacement segments (commercial, 2-wheeler, farm); US PCR and TBR channel build-out underway with orders booked; agri radials growing on low base in US and EU.
segment / subsidiary detail: Replacement: Double-digit growth led by commercial vehicles and 2-wheelers; OEM: Muted growth due to capacity constraints in TBR; International: Healthy double-digit growth (not 20%+), constrained by container shortages and freight hikes; EV: ~30% market share in 2W/3W EV OEMs; Off-Highway: 42+ new SKUs launched; Premium PC/UV: 95% coverage of BMW/Audi/Mercedes range; Rural demand recovering with monsoons.
growth verticals / optionality: US market entry (TBR shipping now, PCR launching Q4FY25/Q1FY26); agri radial expansion in US/EU; EV OEM nominations from international players expected in 3-4 quarters; Ambernath Phase 2 expansion (160 tons) gaining traction; digital platform monetization via distributor/fleet apps.
margins & cost dynamics: Gross margin contracted 184 bps YoY and 306 bps QoQ due to 5% QoQ RM increase; natural rubber surged to INR207/kg (13-year high); crude derivatives range-bound; freight costs up 3-4x; pricing hikes of 2.3-2.5% in commercial, 2.5-3% in passenger, 1% in 2W implemented; additional 3-4% hikes expected in Q2 to offset RM and freight pressures; EPR treated as operational cost (not RM).
capex / expansion: INR254cr spent in Q1FY25 (vs INR1,000cr annual guidance); Chennai TBR expansion on track for Q2 completion; Ambernath plant at 70% utilization (105 tons); Phase 2 (160 tons) in planning; light-out certification underway at Chennai (following Halol); AI/ML for predictive quality implemented.
capital allocation: Capex fully funded by internal accruals; negative working capital of INR240cr; debt/EBITDA at 1.1x, debt/equity at 0.4x; no dividend or buyback mentioned; focus on reinvestment in R&D, marketing, and capacity expansion; no external fund-raise planned.
risks & watch-items: Sustained high natural rubber prices (>INR200/kg); prolonged container/freight bottlenecks in exports; competitive price discounting in TBR; EPR cost uncertainty; margin compression if pricing lags RM inflation; geopolitical risks in LATAM/EU; EV adoption slowdown.
management quality / tone: Confident and proactive; management emphasizes pricing discipline, product superiority, and long-term brand building; dismisses competitor discounting; highlights innovation, digital transformation, and sustainability as core differentiators; tone is bullish on growth despite near-term margin headwinds.
non-obvious takeaways: CEAT's digital engagement metrics show 45% organic website traffic growth, 5x increase from premium SUV users, and 140% higher post engagement — indicating successful premium brand repositioning; AI-driven predictive quality is a first in continuous process industry; 37% renewable energy usage at plants is ahead of peers; EPR reversal of INR7cr was exceptional, not structural.

themes.title: Auto OEM cycle - CV replacement & PV premiumization
themes.need: GST 2.0 rate rationalization plus an aged CV fleet still frames the replacement cycle, but Q1FY27's real signal is 2W OEMs EXPANDING margin through a commodity shock. TVSMOTOR sold 1.63mn units (+28%) on INR 13,896cr revenue (+38%) while lifting EBITDA margin 30bps to 12.8% having absorbed a ~4% commodity shock with only ~1.5% of price increase (CARE upgraded it AA+ to AAA), and committed 2W capacity from 6.8mn to 8.3mn by Q4FY27. BAJAJ-AUTO set volume/revenue/EBITDA records with margin at 20.9% (+110bps) through ~4.5% commodity inflation AND ~10% of volume lost to a ransomware shutdown, with EV now 30% of domestic revenue at double-digit EBITDA and Chetak EBITDA-positive - a scaled, profitable EV second engine. Commercial mobility is electrifying fastest: TVSMOTOR's 3W EV penetration crossed 40% for the first time. ASHOKLEY's all-time-high CV volumes (220k units, MHCV share 30.8%) carry the CV leg with defence + Switch EV optionality; TMCV/TMPV/SMLMAH/ESCORTS on CV/tractors; APOLLOTYRE/JKTYRE/BALKRISIND/MRF on tyres.
themes.driver: Capacity commissioning against demand (TVSMOTOR 2W to 8.3mn by Q4FY27, BAJAJ-AUTO 7m to 9m+ units); 3W/2W EV penetration inflection; GST-2.0 price-cut demand, aged-fleet replacement and festive 2W/PV.
